0. Overview

In this practical example, we will use two factors (i) number of factors (Lv) and (ii) factor dissimilarity (dissim) to predict soil decomposition rate (Decom), with the dataset CombinedData.csv.

Goal

  • Explain what linear regressions estimate
  • Fit simple linear regression and extend to multiple regression
  • Diagnose model assumptions and use robust SEs if needed
  • Compare models (ANOVA, AIC/BIC, ΔR²) and report results clearly

What we use from the data

  • Decom: Soil decomposition rate (response variable).
  • Lv: factor level: number of factors acting simultaneously (numerical predictor).
  • dissim: factor dissimilarity, an index measures how dissimilar the co-acting factors are (continuous predictor)

1. Subsetting data for regression analysis

# Keep only variables used in regression analysis and drop missing values
dat2 <- dat %>% dplyr::select(Decom, Lv, dissim) %>% drop_na()

nrow(dat2)
## [1] 343
summary(dat2)
##      Decom              Lv            dissim

2. Understand data patterns

# Distribution of Decom
ggplot(dat2, aes(Decom)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 30) +
  labs(title = "Distribution of Decomposition Rate (Decom)")

# Scatter with linear smoother: Decom ~ n_factors
ggplot(dat2, aes(Lv, Decom)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.6, position = position_jitter(width = 0.05, height = 0)) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = TRUE) +
  labs(x = "Number of factors", y = "Decom",
       title = "Decomposition vs. Number of Factors")
## `geom_smooth()` using formula = 'y ~ x'

# Optional: pairs plot to see relationships & correlations
GGally::ggpairs(dat2, columns = c("dissim","Lv","Decom"))

3. Build simple linear model

Model formular:

Decom ~ Lv Predict soil decomposition rate from factor number lv.

m1 <- lm(Decom ~ Lv, data = dat2)

summary(m1)     # Coefs, p-values, R²
## 
## Call:
## lm(formula = Decom ~ Lv, data = dat2)
## 
## Residuals:
##       Min        1Q    Median        3Q       Max 
## -0.192035 -0.021474 -0.000894  0.021596  0.138152 
## 
## Coefficients:
##               Estimate Std. Error t value Pr(>|t|)    
## (Intercept)  0.6673085  0.0030802 216.644  < 2e-16 ***
## Lv          -0.0063842  0.0008416  -7.586 3.17e-13 ***
## ---
## Signif. codes:  0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1
## 
## Residual standard error: 0.0401 on 341 degrees of freedom
## Multiple R-squared:  0.1444, Adjusted R-squared:  0.1419 
## F-statistic: 57.55 on 1 and 341 DF,  p-value: 3.168e-13
confint(m1)     # 95% CIs
##                    2.5 %       97.5 %
## (Intercept)  0.661249856  0.673367074
## Lv          -0.008039472 -0.004728868
broom::glance(m1)[c("r.squared","adj.r.squared","AIC","BIC")]
## # A tibble: 1 × 4
##   r.squared adj.r.squared    AIC    BIC
##       <dbl>         <dbl>  <dbl>  <dbl>
## 1     0.144         0.142 -1229. -1218.

Interpret

  • Slop (effect of Lv): expected change in Soil decomposition rate per +1 factor.
  • Report estimate, 95% CI, and p-value.
  • Model fit: R^2 tells you the proportion of variance in Decom explained by Lv.

4. Assumptions & diagnostics for m1

# Base diagnostic plots
par(mfrow = c(2,2)); plot(m1); par(mfrow = c(1,1))

# Tests (use judiciously; plots first!)
lmtest::bptest(m1)            # heteroscedasticity (p < .05 => non-constant variance)
## 
##  studentized Breusch-Pagan test
## 
## data:  m1
## BP = 56.42, df = 1, p-value = 5.852e-14
car::ncvTest(m1)              # similar purpose
## Non-constant Variance Score Test 
## Variance formula: ~ fitted.values 
## Chisquare = 131.0453, Df = 1, p = < 2.22e-16
# If heteroscedastic: report robust SEs (coefficients unchanged, SEs/p-values adjust)
lmtest::coeftest(m1, vcov = sandwich::vcovHC(m1, type = "HC1"))
## 
## t test of coefficients:
## 
##               Estimate Std. Error  t value  Pr(>|t|)    
## (Intercept)  0.6673085  0.0025252 264.2632 < 2.2e-16 ***
## Lv          -0.0063842  0.0012135  -5.2608  2.54e-07 ***
## ---
## Signif. codes:  0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1

What to look for:

  • Residuals vs Fitted ~ no clear curve (linearity).
  • Scale-Location ~ fairly horizontal band (constant variance).
  • Q-Q plot ~ residuals ~ straight line (approx. normal distribution).
  • Cook’s distance ~ any very influential points?

5. Multiple regression (add factor dissimilarity index)

Model formular:

Decom ~ Lv + dissim Predict soil decomposition rate with two predictors lv and dissim.

m2 <- lm(Decom ~ Lv + dissim, data = dat2) # build multiple regression model from two predictors

summary(m2)
## 
## Call:
## lm(formula = Decom ~ Lv + dissim, data = dat2)
## 
## Residuals:
##       Min        1Q    Median        3Q       Max 
## -0.191693 -0.022074  0.000972  0.019407  0.145637 
## 
## Coefficients:
##              Estimate Std. Error t value Pr(>|t|)    
## (Intercept)  0.665849   0.003018 220.598  < 2e-16 ***
## Lv          -0.001760   0.001331  -1.322    0.187    
## dissim      -0.048874   0.011086  -4.408  1.4e-05 ***
## ---
## Signif. codes:  0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1
## 
## Residual standard error: 0.03905 on 340 degrees of freedom
## Multiple R-squared:  0.1907, Adjusted R-squared:  0.1859 
## F-statistic: 40.05 on 2 and 340 DF,  p-value: 2.412e-16
confint(m2)
##                    2.5 %        97.5 %
## (Intercept)  0.659912366  0.6717864839
## Lv          -0.004378657  0.0008580838
## dissim      -0.070681016 -0.0270675660
broom::glance(m2)[c("r.squared","adj.r.squared","AIC","BIC")]
## # A tibble: 1 × 4
##   r.squared adj.r.squared    AIC    BIC
##       <dbl>         <dbl>  <dbl>  <dbl>
## 1     0.191         0.186 -1246. -1231.

Compare m1 vs m2

Does adding another predictor dissim improve explanatory power beyond Lv?

anova(m1, m2)   # nested F-test: significant p => m2 improves fit
## Analysis of Variance Table
## 
## Model 1: Decom ~ Lv
## Model 2: Decom ~ Lv + dissim
##   Res.Df     RSS Df Sum of Sq      F    Pr(>F)    
## 1    341 0.54823                                  
## 2    340 0.51859  1  0.029643 19.434 1.398e-05 ***
## ---
## Signif. codes:  0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1
glance_m1 <- broom::glance(m1)
glance_m2 <- broom::glance(m2)
delta_r2 <- glance_m2$r.squared - glance_m1$r.squared
delta_r2
## [1] 0.04626221

Diagnostic for m2

par(mfrow = c(2,2)); plot(m2); par(mfrow = c(1,1))

lmtest::bptest(m2)
## 
##  studentized Breusch-Pagan test
## 
## data:  m2
## BP = 47.369, df = 2, p-value = 5.176e-11
lmtest::coeftest(m2, vcov = sandwich::vcovHC(m2, type = "HC1"))  # robust SEs if needed
## 
## t test of coefficients:
## 
##               Estimate Std. Error  t value  Pr(>|t|)    
## (Intercept)  0.6658494  0.0025043 265.8870 < 2.2e-16 ***
## Lv          -0.0017603  0.0014635  -1.2028    0.2299    
## dissim      -0.0488743  0.0117669  -4.1536 4.145e-05 ***
## ---
## Signif. codes:  0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1
# Influence points (rule-of-thumb threshold)
cooksd <- cooks.distance(m2)
which(cooksd > 4/length(cooksd))

6. Visualizing partial effects

# Effect of n_factors (holding dissim at mean)
new_nf <- tibble(
  Lv = seq(min(dat2$Lv), max(dat2$Lv), length.out = 100),
  dissim    = mean(dat2$dissim, na.rm = TRUE)
)
pred_nf <- cbind(new_nf, predict(m2, newdata = new_nf, se.fit = TRUE)) %>%
  as_tibble() %>% mutate(lwr = fit - 1.96*se.fit, upr = fit + 1.96*se.fit)

ggplot() +
  geom_point(data = dat2, aes(Lv, Decom), alpha = 0.4) +
  geom_line(data = pred_nf, aes(Lv, fit)) +
  geom_ribbon(data = pred_nf, aes(Lv, ymin = lwr, ymax = upr), alpha = 0.2) +
  labs(title = "Partial effect of number of factors on Decom (dissim at mean)",
       x = "Number of factors", y = "Predicted Decom")

# Effect of dissim (holding n_factors at mean)
new_ds <- tibble(
  dissim    = seq(min(dat2$dissim), max(dat2$dissim), length.out = 100),
  Lv = mean(dat2$Lv, na.rm = TRUE)
)
pred_ds <- cbind(new_ds, predict(m2, newdata = new_ds, se.fit = TRUE)) %>%
  as_tibble() %>% mutate(lwr = fit - 1.96*se.fit, upr = fit + 1.96*se.fit)

ggplot() +
  geom_point(data = dat2, aes(dissim, Decom), alpha = 0.4) +
  geom_line(data = pred_ds, aes(dissim, fit)) +
  geom_ribbon(data = pred_ds, aes(dissim, ymin = lwr, ymax = upr), alpha = 0.2) +
  labs(title = "Partial effect of dissimilarity on Decom (n_factors at mean)",
       x = "Factor dissimilarity", y = "Predicted Decom")
